notice.exec.window_failed: The plan step's window on {server} did not open ({reason}) — its changes are checked as usual.
notice.exec.window_unclosed: The plan step's window on {server} did not close ({reason}) — its changes are checked as usual.
notice.monitor.window_applied: Plan step: into the baseline on {servers} — {accepted}.
notice.monitor.window_unchanged: The plan step changed nothing the monitor checks on {servers}.
notice.monitor.window_partial: Plan step: not everything on {servers} went into the baseline ({detail}).
notice.monitor.window_dangerous: Plan step: dangerous changes are not taken into the baseline — {objects}; they open incidents.
notice.monitor.window_rejected: Plan step: the changes on {servers} are not in the baseline ({detail}) — they are checked as usual.
notice.monitor.window_expired: The plan step's window on {server} did not close in 30 minutes — changes are checked as usual.
notice.release.healthy: ✅ Release {rev}: the checks after the release passed ({checks})
notice.release.reinstall_uncovered: ⚠️ Release {rev}: {agents} still run the old instructions — no reinstall was requested ({why}). To reinstall, as root on the host: kd-cabinet operation request --agents {agents_csv}
notice.pipeline.missing_next_step: ⚠️ A turn of {agent} ended without a next step — nobody is on the card now.
notice.pipeline.continuation_limit: ⚠️ Automatic continuations of {agent} stopped at the limit with no verified result — please take a look.
notice.pipeline.wait_needs_routing: ⚠️ What {agent} waits for is gone or ended without the answer it needed — decide who is next.
notice.pipeline.outcome_refused: ⚠️ The outcome {agent} recorded could not apply — a next step is needed.
notice.pipeline.assist_failed: ⚠️ The help {agent} asked for ended without a result — sort out the cause.
notice.pipeline.assist_stalled: ⚠️ The help {agent} asked for has had no answer for an hour — check on the helper.
notice.pipeline.stage_missing: ⚠️ An approved stage of the brief has no card — your look is needed.
notice.pipeline.stage_cancelled: ⚠️ A stage's card was closed without the work — the plan has a hole, decide what is next.
notice.pipeline.stage_reopened: ⚠️ A closed stage of the chain plan is back in work — the stages after it build on its commits, decide whether to pause them.
notice.pipeline.stage_held: ⏸ The stage waits for your decision: {reason}
notice.pipeline.stage_boss_silent: ⏸ BOSS did not decide on the stage in 30 minutes — the stage waits for your decision.
notice.pipeline.stage_boss_absent: ⏸ BOSS is not available — the stage waits for your decision.
notice.pipeline.stage_review_failed: ⏸ The stage's code review did not happen ({reason}) — the stage waits for your decision.
notice.pipeline.release_degraded: ⛔ The card's release failed its check — {agent} holds it.
notice.pipeline.council_failed: ⚠️ The card's council did not gather — no critic could start.
notice.pipeline.council_run_failed: ⚠️ A critic of the council failed — the cause is in the «Council» block.
notice.pipeline.council_stalled: ⚠️ {agent} has not answered the council's findings for an hour — check on the executor.
notice.pipeline.council_unanswered: ⚠️ {agent} handed the work in with council findings unanswered.
notice.council.decision_failed: ⚠️ The council on PR #{number} is over, but its decision did not open. Ask the developer to publish the pull request again.
notice.council.failed: ⚠️ The council did not gather: no critic could start (round {round}). The work goes on without it.
notice.brief.size_s_started: ▶️ Brief v{version} of size S started without «Approve»: {agent} took the card. Send it back with a message in the thread or to the Inbox.
notice.brief.size_s_operations: Brief v{version} of size S waits for «Approve»: it has operations.
notice.brief.size_s_stages: Brief v{version} of size S waits for «Approve»: it has stages.
notice.brief.size_s_servers: Brief v{version} of size S waits for «Approve»: it is work on servers.
notice.brief.size_s_blocked: Brief v{version} of size S waits for «Approve»: it cannot start right away (dependencies, the taker or its specialization).
notice.defer.due: ⏰ The time the card was put off until has come ({until}): no agent holds it in work — please take a look.
notice.watch.recovered: ⚠️ The jam state was damaged: set aside and rebuilt.
notice.factory.unknown: ⛔ The session host lost the reinstall of {agents} (operation {operation}): whether the roles are installed is unknown. Check as root on the host: new_agent.sh --verify <agent> (0 — the role matches the code); to retry, kd-cabinet operation request --agents {agents}; a role's pause — kd-session-host status, lift it with kd-session-host resume <agent>.
notice.factory.failed_resumed: ⚠️ Reinstalling {agents} did not run (operation {operation}): stage {stage} · {reason}. Nothing was installed; the roles work as before. To retry: {retry} (or as root on the host: kd-cabinet operation request --agents {agents}).
notice.factory.failed_resumed_root: ⚠️ Reinstalling {agents} did not run (operation {operation}): stage {stage} · {reason}. Nothing was installed; the roles work as before. To retry, as root on the host: kd-cabinet operation request --agents {agents}.
notice.factory.done: ✅ Reinstalled {agents} at revision {revision} (operation {operation}): checks passed, work goes on.
notice.factory.component_unknown: ⛔ The session host lost {component} {mode} (operation {operation}): whether the script ran is unknown. Check with a {component} check request (if the catalog has one) or as root on the host.
notice.devcheck.passed: ✅ The check of PR #{pr} ({project}, {head}) passed: {profiles} in {duration}. Log: kd-host-read tail -n 200 {log}.
notice.devcheck.superseded: ℹ️ The check of PR #{pr} ({project}, {head}) was dropped: the PR has a new head.
notice.devcheck.cancelled: ℹ️ The check of PR #{pr} ({project}, {head}) was cancelled ({reason}).
notice.devcheck.host_lost: ⚠️ The session host lost the check of PR #{pr} ({project}, {head}) (operation {operation}): the result is unknown — ask for the check again.

deploys.launch.title: Deploy {project} · {env}
deploys.launch.sign_note: Confirm with your passkey — no PIN or fingerprint. The signature lasts 10 minutes and starts the deploy once; if the branch moves on, the launch is refused.
mon.accepted_waiting: Accepted into the baseline — waiting for the monitor
mon.revoked_waiting: Access removed — waiting for the monitor
mon.group.title: {title} · servers: {servers}
mon.bulk.too_many: At most {max} per signature: {n} more with the next one
inbox.bundle: Accept into the baseline — objects: {n}, servers: {servers}
mon.analysis_pending: The automatic investigation will appear here when the sysadmin replies. You do not need to hand off an incident for initial diagnostics.
mon.explain.certbot: The certificate renewal service failed. Identify the affected domains, check their certificate expiry dates and investigate why renewal failed.
mon.explain.units: Service {unit} failed. Use the service journal and the sysadmin investigation to establish the cause and impact on the server.
push.test.incident_body: Tapping should open this exact incident. This is a link test, not a new alert.
mon.data_attention: Data needs rechecking: freshness is not confirmed
mon.baseline_help: The baseline contains accepted objects and values used to detect changes. Being listed does not confirm availability.
mon.baseline_warning: Capture a new baseline for {server}: ports, peers and settings. Accepted SSH identities are retained. Current changes become expected. Collection can take several minutes; signing does not mean application succeeded.
mon.global_addresses: Trusted addresses are shared by all servers. Adding or removing changes the global list.
mon.search_objects: Find an address, key, port or peer
mon.alerts.title: Platform alerts
mon.alerts.hint: Failures of the platform's own services, releases and operations — with no card. The “Alert” and “Attention” notifications lead here.
mon.alerts.none_recent: No alerts in the last 7 days.
mon.recommend_investigation: Ask the sysadmin to investigate and propose a resolution
mon.handoff_help: Create a linked card with the server, incident and observation. The sysadmin receives a read-only investigation. Server changes require separate plan approval.
mon.recheck_queued: Server recheck queued; results will appear after polling
mon.ask.title: What is needed from you
mon.ask.card: The work goes on in card {card} · {assignee}.
mon.ask.accepting: You accepted the change at {at}. The monitor applies it on its next check, in a few minutes, and closes the incident — nothing else is needed from you.
mon.ask.revoking: You signed «access removed» at {at}. On its next check the monitor compares the server's snapshot and closes the incident if the key no longer lets anyone in — the key does not become trusted.
mon.ask.revoke_failed: The monitor did not close the incident as «access removed»: {detail}. Remove the key from the server and sign again — or accept the login if it is yours.
mon.ask.confirm_login_revoke_hint: The access is already gone (the key removed, the account deleted) — «Access removed»: the incident closes, the key does not become trusted.
mon.ask.accept_failed: The monitor could not apply the last acceptance: {detail}. Accept again or hand it to the sysadmin.
mon.ask.confirm_change_hint: Yes — the monitor takes what is there now as normal and the incident closes. No — the sysadmin finds out who changed what.
mon.ask.confirm_login_hint: Yes — the key becomes trusted, name whose it is. No — the sysadmin looks into the login.
mon.ask.not_mine: The owner does not recognise this change: find out who changed what.
mon.ask.review_report: The sysadmin investigated the incident: read the investigation above and decide whether work is needed.
mon.ask.investigating: The sysadmin investigates on their own — nothing is needed from you yet. Anything to add — hand it over with a comment.
mon.ask.wait_recovery: The monitor waits for recovery: the incident closes by itself. If it needs a hand, hand it to the sysadmin.
mon.change.again: Changes since the opening: {count}, the last at {at}.
mon.accept.what: What is on the server now is accepted: the monitor stops counting it as a difference and the incident closes as an accepted change.
mon.revoke.what: The key does not become trusted. The monitor compares the latest snapshot of {server}: while any authorized_keys there still holds the key, the incident stays open; otherwise it closes as «access removed». A new login with this key opens a new incident.
mon.quiet.until_closed: Reminders are off until it closes; a worse level still reminds.
mon.quiet.help: No reminders about this incident. A worse level still reminds.
mon.resolution.revoke: Closed: access removed, the key not trusted
mon.explain.masked: A unit file linked to /dev/null blocks activation (masked). This differs from the accepted baseline. The observation alone does not identify who changed it, why, or whether the service is needed.
mon.explain.drift: Settings differ from the accepted baseline. This can be an expected or unwanted change. A hash shows a difference but cannot explain contents or impact; investigate.
mon.explain.reboot: The monitor observes a pending reboot after a kernel update. The age is the observed waiting time. Ask the sysadmin to propose a suitable window and plan.
mon.explain.login: An SSH login or identity is outside the accepted set. Establish who owns the access and whether it was expected.
mon.explain.object: An object is outside the accepted baseline. Verify its purpose and origin before accepting it.
mon.explain.collection: Some monitoring data cannot be collected reliably. Service health is not confirmed.
mon.explain.threshold: The check detected a deviation from its configured rule. The value and measurement time are shown above; user impact needs investigation.
mon.never_measured: An expected check has not reported results yet
mon.transfer_existing: Return to Inbox and assign a read-only investigation to sysadmin
mon.resolution.unknown: Closed: the legacy record does not specify why
mon.disable_help: Disabling a check stops its collection and closes its incidents as 'Check disabled'. It does not verify server recovery.
mon.monitor_stale: No recent full monitoring cycle is confirmed. A partial server check does not confirm fleet-wide collection.
mon.accept_login_title: Accept event {id} without trusting the login method
mon.weak_login_help: This login to {server} has no verified key. Accepting the event does not add an identity to the baseline or trust the login method. Investigate the insecure method separately.
mon.baseline_unavailable: The monitoring baseline is unavailable or corrupt. Comparison is limited; the lists below may be from an earlier sync.
mon.delivery_backlog: Queues at the last cycle: {n} notifications, {changes} cabinet changes
hindsight.settings_hint: Service status, memory banks, updates and usage
hindsight.not_installed: Hindsight is not installed on this host: the agents have no long-term memory and carry only their notes (memory/notes.md) across sessions. To turn it on: "hindsight": true in the overlay's host/install.json, then the hindsight install phase and the agents reinstalled.
hindsight.no_snapshot: The collector has not provided a diagnostic snapshot yet.
hindsight.refresh_hint: The collector checks the server every 5 minutes. This page reads its snapshot every minute; the button reads it immediately.
hindsight.stale: Data is stale or has not arrived. Current Hindsight status is unknown; check digipaddock-hindsight-status.timer.
hindsight.backup_hint: An active backup timer does not confirm a successful backup or a recoverable database.
hindsight.server_manual: An administrator upgrades the server during maintenance. Version checks install nothing.
hindsight.latest: Published versions: server {server}, plugin {client}. Checked: {at}. Checked daily against PyPI and npm.
hindsight.bank_model: A bank is a separate memory area. Agents are currently connected by their working directories. An agent bank may contain knowledge from multiple projects.
hindsight.incomplete: The full bank list could not be retrieved.
hindsight.activity: Bank requests over the last 7 days
hindsight.no_activity: The audit log is available; no requests in this period.
hindsight.audit_off: The audit log is disabled or unsupported. Request counts are unknown.
hindsight.project_binding_hint: The sessions of a bound project's cards read and write its bank; the cards of a project without one and the agent's chat use the assignee's role bank. Set the bank in Projects. Routing cards to an agent does not choose a bank.
hindsight.ingestion_hint: Settings from installed client configs. Running sessions pick up changes when the relevant process restarts. Page schedules use server cron; H spreads refreshes across pages.
hindsight.no_spend_data: No spend data available for this period
hindsight.spend_hint: Internal model calls, distinct from agents accessing memory. kd-usage records daily totals; today may not be available yet. Missing data is not zero spend. List-price estimates are not separate invoices when using a subscription.
hindsight.web_unconfigured: The web interface URL is not configured. This does not prove it is disabled: the API and web interface are separate components. An administrator can set hindsight_web_url in cabinet.json after configuring access.
contours.title: Check contours
context.intro: When a session's conversation grows to the limit, Claude Code compacts it into a summary and goes on with the turn. Each role has its own limit; a new value applies from the role's next session start (fresh or resumed) and its jobs, with no reinstall. Too low a limit hurts: after a compaction the agent loses what it has already tried.
context.invalid: A whole number of tokens from 100,000 to 1,000,000 — or tick «No limit»
models.key_setup_required: Key signing is not set up yet: root must enroll your passkey — kd-model-keys enroll {user}
models.key_help: One key per provider, shared by its models. Saving and deleting require a passkey signature.
models.key_delete_confirm: Delete the {provider} key? New runs of this provider’s models will fail because the key is missing.
models.key_audit_failed: Key changed, but its feed event could not be recorded. Contact the administrator.
models.subscription_help: The claude setup-token credential for agents, worker jobs and Hindsight. Replacement only. Hindsight restarts automatically after replacement.
models.subscription_age: Age: {days} days. Estimated expiry: {expires} (365 days after installation).
models.subscription_warning: Estimated expiry in {days} days. Replace the token in advance.
models.subscription_expired: Estimated lifetime has elapsed. Check the subscription and replace the token.
models.subscription_restart_failed: Token saved, but Hindsight could not restart. Contact the administrator.
